summary: An 80-foot steel Aermotor tower built in 1921 at Grove Mountain and moved to Brook Mountain in 1940 or 1941; registered 2017 and still standing.

access.note: A gate on the service road stops vehicles. Hikers walk the gated road from Brooks Run Road. No source found on climbing the tower itself.

visit.trail_note: Park at the intersection of Brooks Run Road and Ridge Road, not in front of the gate. Walk the gated service road, an easy 1.9-mile out-and-back per the trail listing.

events.note: Built as a steel Aermotor tower at Grove Mountain in Cameron County
Move announced for summer 1940. The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says it moved in 1940.
The National Historic Lookout Register says the tower was relocated to the Brooks Run site in 1941 and lists 1941 under Built.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, December 6, 2017

corrections.proposed: 1921 built at Grove Mountain; relocated to Brooks Run in 1940 or 1941
corrections.why: 1941 is the relocation date the NHLR gives for the Brooks Run site, not the original build. The 1921 build year comes from the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry for Grove Mountain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites entry says the tower moved in 1940, and the June 1940 report announced a summer move. The NHLR says it was relocated in 1941. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.
The NHLR names the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry. The trail listing says the Forest Service uses the access road. The story reports the register's agency name.

notes_for_editor: The record's built 1941 is a relocation date. Relocation year is disputed (1940 vs 1941). No current staffing status or climbing rule was found. The trail listing's operational wording is the only current-status evidence, and it is a hiking site, not an agency.
